steps.body: Seven plus three fills the shown ten-frame. Completing ten creates an easy landmark.
steps.narration: Seven plus three fills the shown ten-frame. Completing ten creates an easy landmark.

widget.prompt: You have 8 in the frame. Add enough to make ten.

commonCounts.feedback: One more square is not enough; keep filling until every square is full.

widget.missFeedback: Fill one square at a time, counting as you go.
widget.successFeedback: Ten filled — 8 needed 2 more to make a whole ten.

predict.prompt: 8 is in the frame. How many more are needed to make a whole ten?
predict.reveal: Ten take away 8 is 2 — exactly how many squares are still empty. Answering 8 just echoes the count already in the frame; the question asks for the missing part, not the part you can see.

widget.prompt: Which split of six lets six plus six complete ten first?

options.label: 4 and 2
options.feedback: Correct — 4 completes ten and 2 remains to add on.

options.label: 2 and 5
options.feedback: Those parts do not total 6, so the split loses or invents counters.

options.label: 6 and 0
options.feedback: This split is based on the first addend rather than on what ten still needs.

options.label: 5 and 1
options.feedback: Taking 5 would pass ten instead of completing it exactly. Use only 4.
